overview: The paper proposes Iterative Error Correction (IEC), a plug-and-play test-time method that mitigates approximation errors in efficient diffusion models (quantized/cached) by iteratively refining the model's output at each timestep, transforming exponential error accumulation into linear growth without retraining or architectural changes.

modules.name: DDIM Sampling Framework
modules.description: Implements the deterministic DDIM sampling process with coefficient computation (At, Bt) for the reverse diffusion process, providing the base denoising trajectory upon which error correction is applied.

modules.name: Error Propagation Analyzer
modules.description: Implements the theoretical analysis of error accumulation across timesteps, including computation of the spectral norm ∥At + BtJt∥ and the recursive error propagation formula to quantify exponential error growth in efficient models.

modules.name: IEC Core Algorithm
modules.description: Implements the Iterative Error Correction method with fixed-point iteration: initializes the estimate via standard DDIM update, then iteratively refines using the contraction mapping G(x) with convergence check (threshold τ, max iterations K) and hyperparameter λ.

modules.name: Contraction Mapping Verifier
modules.description: Computes the Jacobian of the mapping G(x) and verifies the contraction condition ∥∇G(x)∥ < 1 by evaluating ∥(1-λ)I + λBtJt∥ across timesteps and λ values, ensuring Banach fixed-point theorem convergence guarantees.

modules.name: Timestep-wise Network Quantization
modules.description: Implements timestep-aware quantization for diffusion models (W4A8 and W8A8 configurations), including channel-wise weight quantization, layer-wise activation quantization, and optional local reconstruction for low-bit scenarios.

modules.name: Feature Caching Module
modules.description: Implements DeepCache-style feature caching that reuses pre-computed intermediate features across adjacent diffusion timesteps, with configurable cache interval N and block-level caching strategies for different model architectures.

modules.name: CacheQuant Hybrid Integration
modules.description: Combines quantization and feature caching into a unified efficient inference pipeline, managing the interaction between quantized model forward passes and cached feature reuse across timesteps.

modules.name: Dataset Loading and Preprocessing
modules.description: Handles data loading and preprocessing for CIFAR-10, LSUN-Churchs, LSUN-Bedrooms, ImageNet, and MS-COCO datasets, including image resizing, normalization, and text prompt extraction for text-to-image generation.

modules.name: Diffusion Model Wrappers
modules.description: Provides unified wrappers for DDPM, LDM, and Stable Diffusion architectures, standardizing forward pass interfaces and noise prediction outputs to enable consistent application of IEC across different model types.

modules.name: Selective Timestep Application
modules.description: Implements the flexible IEC application strategy that selectively applies error correction to subsets of timesteps (e.g., first/last ±1/4, ±1/8, ±1/10, ±1/20), enabling fine-grained trade-off between quality improvement and computational overhead.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics Suite
modules.description: Computes all evaluation metrics used in the paper: FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), IS (Inception Score), and CLIP Score (ViT-g/14), with standardized evaluation protocols for 50k-sample and 5k-sample generation settings.

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Orchestrates controlled ablation experiments including: IEC applied to all vs. partial timesteps, varying iteration counts K, comparison with naively increasing diffusion steps, and interaction with different efficiency technique configurations.

modules.name: Hyperparameter Sensitivity Analyzer
modules.description: Systematically evaluates the effect of λ on convergence (verifying ∥∇G(x)∥ < 1) and generation quality across different efficiency techniques, and studies the impact of K (maximum iterations) on performance gains versus computational cost.

modules.name: Computational Overhead Profiler
modules.description: Measures and compares inference time overhead of IEC across different application strategies (all steps, partial steps, varying K), computes overhead percentages relative to baseline efficient models, and generates efficiency-quality trade-off tables.

modules.name: Visualization and Report Generation
modules.description: Generates side-by-side visual comparisons of generated images (baseline vs. efficient model vs. efficient+IEC), produces error accumulation curves across timesteps, spectral norm plots, and automated LaTeX result tables for all experimental configurations.
